title: Deep Herschel observations of the 2 Jy sample: assessing the non-thermal and AGN contributions to the far-IR continuum
question: Assess the incidence of non-thermal synchrotron contamination and the role of AGN radiative heating in the far-IR continuum of a complete sample of 46 powerful 2Jy radio AGN.

what.value: Spitzer MIPS 24 and 70 um fluxes and high frequency VLA/ATCA radio core data

evidence.quote: In addition to the new photometric results, for completeness we also present 24 and 70$\mu$m fluxes from (cite: dicken08) in Table [\[tab:1\]](#tab:1).

our *Spitzer* programme (cite: dicken08), which first determined the SEDs for the 2Jy sample objects, including mid- to far-IR photometry and high frequency radio core data from the *VLA* and *ATCA* observatories.

evidence.quote: The SEDs now include *Spitzer* IRS spectra from 5 to 30$\mu$m presented in (cite: dicken12)

what.value: mm flux measurements for PKS0023-26 and PKS1934-63

evidence.quote: To complement the LABOCA results we also added flux measurements from the literature: mm data from (cite: steppe95) and (cite: partridge16) for PKS0023-26 and PKS1934-63 respectively.

recipe.goal: Measure Herschel PACS and SPIRE far-IR photometry and deblend confused sources
recipe.method: Processed PACS images in HIPE 14.2 with ScanmapPhotProject using aperture photometry (10 or 5 arcsec radius); extracted SPIRE fluxes from level 2 archive products with sourceExtractorSussextractor PRF fitting; deblended confused sources using GetSources.
key_parameters: PACS apertures: 10 arcsec radius (or 5 arcsec for faint <20 mJy / confused sources); 48 blank sky apertures for uncertainty
assumptions: Power-law continuum SED (F_nu proportional to nu^-alpha) iterated from 250 and 350 um fluxes for SPIRE colour/aperture corrections

recipe.goal: Measure APEX LABOCA 870 um sub-mm continuum fluxes
recipe.method: Reduced chopped photometry scans with CRUSH and performed circular aperture photometry (49 arcsec diameter) on maps for two sources (PKS0023-26 and PKS2135-20).
key_parameters: 49 arcsec diameter circular aperture (2.5 beam FWHM) and 8 blank sky apertures for map photometry

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA ~100 GHz non-thermal core continuum fluxes
recipe.method: Measured peak mJy/beam flux of the point-like core from standard pipeline-processed average continuum images from the ALMA archive.
assumptions: Cores are point-like within the 1.4-3.7 arcsec ALMA beam and absolute flux calibration uncertainty is ~5%

recipe.goal: Construct radio-to-IR SEDs and classify/correct non-thermal synchrotron contamination
recipe.method: Constructed radio-to-IR SEDs, classified sources as dominated (D), potentially contaminated (P), or correctable (C) for lobe/hotspot and core emission in <200 um and >200 um bands, and subtracted power-law extrapolations of radio/mm/sub-mm data for 6 C-class objects.
key_parameters: Criterion for potential core contamination (P): highest frequency radio-to-sub-mm core flux > 50% of the far-IR flux
assumptions: Non-thermal core SED remains flat up to far-IR wavelengths for P classification; power-law shape for C subtraction

recipe.goal: Compute rest-frame 100 and 160 um luminosities and test correlations with AGN power indicators
recipe.method: Calculated rest-frame L_100 and L_160 with modified black-body K-corrections, and computed Spearman rank and partial rank correlation coefficients against L_[OIII] and L_24 across sub-samples.
key_parameters: Modified black-body emissivity index beta = 1.2; 100 Monte Carlo iterations for 160 um upper limits
assumptions: Cosmology: H_o = 71 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.27, Omega_lambda = 0.73; modified black-body with beta = 1.2

evidence.quote: We find that the overall incidence of non-thermal contamination in the PACS bands ($<$200 $\mu$m) is in the range 28 – 43%; however, this rises to 30 – 72% for wavelengths ($>$200 $\mu$m) sampled by the SPIRE instrument.
